ideas.hypothesis: QE episodes raise firm R&D and later TFP growth by lowering long-term financing costs for innovating firms, partly offsetting the TFP losses attributed to the zero lower bound.

sources.role: mechanism: monetary policy shapes firms' innovation incentives and endogenous TFP; ZLB-induced TFP losses
finding: unconventional policy after 2008 stabilized inflation expectations

ideas.test: US Compustat firms 2005-2016: event study of QE announcements comparing R&D of bond-financed with bank-dependent R&D-intensive firms; then industry TFP growth (NBER-CES) over 3-5 years by QE exposure.
ideas.disconfirming: No difference in R&D response, and TFP growth is no higher in QE-exposed industries.

ideas.hypothesis: Monetary policy passes more strongly to real activity (housing starts, construction jobs) in regions with permissive land use and more strongly to house prices in land-constrained regions.

sources.role: measure: land-use and urban form classifications used in regional research
mechanism: smoothness of the transmission mechanism determines policy effectiveness
mechanism: structural obstacles in the transmission mechanism

ideas.test: US MSA panel with the Wharton land-use regulation index; local projections of housing starts, house prices and employment on identified monetary shocks interacted with regulation, 1990-2019.
ideas.disconfirming: Responses do not differ by land-use stringency.

ideas.hypothesis: More intensive sterilization of foreign exchange inflows lowers exchange rate pass-through to domestic prices, because it limits the money growth that otherwise accompanies currency movements.

sources.role: method/finding: VAR estimates of pass-through and shocks to Chinese prices
measure/method: VECM evaluation of sterilization of FX reserve accumulation

ideas.test: China monthly 2000-2015: rolling estimates of the sterilization coefficient and time-varying VAR estimates of pass-through; regress pass-through on sterilization intensity.
ideas.disconfirming: Pass-through is unrelated to, or rises with, sterilization intensity.

ideas.hypothesis: Fed balance sheet expansions produce larger spillovers to Chinese asset prices and activity than policy-rate changes of equivalent stance.

sources.role: setting: excess reserves and an expanded Fed balance sheet
method: TVP-SVAR of China-US spillovers using asset price indices and activity factors

ideas.test: TVP-SVAR 2002-2019 including Fed total assets and a shadow rate, a Chinese asset price index and activity factor; compare normalized impulse responses to balance sheet and rate shocks.
ideas.disconfirming: Balance sheet shocks spill over no more than rate shocks.

ideas.hypothesis: Reaction functions that respond to headline inflation whatever its source overreact to cost-push inflation and cause larger output losses; successful inflation targeters respond less to the cost-push component.

sources.role: mechanism: appropriate policy differs under demand-pull and cost-push inflation
method: GMM/LIML Taylor-rule estimation for the CBRT

ideas.test: Split Turkish and Nigerian CPI into supply- and demand-driven parts (sign-based decomposition of price and quantity changes); estimate GMM Taylor rules with separate coefficients and relate them to output volatility.
ideas.disconfirming: Coefficients are equal and no added output cost appears.

ideas.hypothesis: Rising fiscal pressure erodes de facto central bank independence, seen in governor turnover and central bank credit to government, mainly where legal independence is weak.

sources.role: setting: fiscal pressure and transfer payments in Romania
mechanism: independence and authority of the central bank for effective transmission
mechanism: strategic interaction between central bank and fiscal authority

ideas.test: Panel of about 30 emerging economies 1995-2018 with deficits and debt, legal CBI indices, governor turnover and central bank claims on government; panel regressions with interactions.
ideas.disconfirming: Fiscal pressure does not predict turnover or monetary financing.

ideas.hypothesis: Stronger interest rate smoothing is followed by higher bank leverage and credit growth, because predictable gradual moves lower perceived risk.

sources.role: mechanism: lean-versus-clean debate and financial fragility
measure: estimated weight on interest rate smoothing in the central bank loss function

ideas.test: Rolling estimates of smoothing parameters for about 20 central banks; panel of credit-to-GDP gaps and bank leverage regressed on lagged smoothing.
ideas.disconfirming: No association between smoothing and later fragility.

ideas.hypothesis: Broad money growth predicted euro area output during the Great Recession better than policy rate-based indicators did.

sources.role: finding: monetarist critique attributing the euro area Great Recession to contractionary policy
setting: role of monetary aggregates in policy

ideas.test: Euro area monthly data 1999-2013; out-of-sample forecasts of industrial production using M3 growth versus Euribor and term spreads; compare RMSE in 2008-2013.
ideas.disconfirming: M3 adds no predictive power.

ideas.hypothesis: Clear forward guidance that lowers interest rate uncertainty raises firm R&D investment.

sources.role: mechanism: slower-than-anticipated tightening benefits TFP; monetary shocks affect R&D
mechanism: communication strategy and credibility

ideas.test: Text-based clarity measure for FOMC statements; quarterly Compustat R&D; panel regressions with rate uncertainty (option-implied) as mediator.
ideas.disconfirming: R&D is unrelated to communication clarity.

ideas.hypothesis: Under discretion, PBoC policy shows a measurable average inflation bias and stabilization bias relative to a commitment counterfactual.

sources.role: method/finding: Bayesian comparison favoring discretion; loss weights; counterfactuals
mechanism: output focus and credibility

ideas.test: Estimate a New Keynesian model for China 1992-2019 under discretion with a free output target; compute the implied bias and compare simulated inflation with commitment.
ideas.disconfirming: The implied bias is close to zero.

ideas.hypothesis: Households in car-dependent, low-density areas have inflation expectations more sensitive to gasoline prices, which raises the volatility of aggregate expectations.

sources.role: mechanism: urban form shapes travel behavior and car use
setting: anchoring of inflation expectations

ideas.test: Michigan Survey or NY Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations microdata with ZIP codes merged with density and car-commute shares; regress expectation revisions on gas price changes x density.
ideas.disconfirming: Sensitivity does not differ by urban form.

ideas.b: central bank of the republic of turkey
ideas.hypothesis: Bayesian comparison of Taylor, hybrid McCallum-Taylor and exchange-rate-augmented rules favors an exchange-rate-augmented rule for the CBRT, contrary to GMM-based results.

sources.role: finding: GMM/LIML support only Taylor-rule specifications for CBRT
method: Bayesian model comparison of policy descriptions

ideas.test: Estimate a small open-economy New Keynesian model for Turkey 2006-2019 with each rule; compare marginal likelihoods.
ideas.disconfirming: The plain Taylor rule has the highest marginal likelihood.

ideas.hypothesis: The VAR price puzzle shrinks when the endogeneity of money supply to credit demand is modeled explicitly.

sources.role: method/finding: VAR showing weak monetary policy effect on prices
mechanism: endogenous money limits central bank control of quantities

ideas.test: VARs for China and the US with and without bank credit demand indicators (loan surveys); compare price impulse responses to policy shocks.
ideas.disconfirming: The price puzzle persists unchanged.

ideas.hypothesis: Where transfer payments make up a larger share of household income, consumption responds less to policy rate changes through the interest rate channel.

sources.role: setting: rising transfer payments in Romania
mechanism: redistributive effects of monetary policy
mechanism: transmission mechanism

ideas.test: EU country panel 2000-2018; local projections of consumption to monetary shocks interacted with the transfer share of disposable income.
ideas.disconfirming: No attenuation with higher transfer shares.

ideas.hypothesis: Crisis-time monetary tightening, as in the IMF prescription for Southeast Asia, caused persistent falls in firm R&D that fed long-run productivity losses.

sources.role: setting: IMF tightening during the Southeast Asian crisis
mechanism: monetary policy and innovation investment

ideas.test: Firm-level data for Korea and Thailand 1995-2005; compare R&D of firms with high and low short-term debt exposure to the rate hikes; difference-in-differences.
ideas.disconfirming: No differential R&D decline.

ideas.hypothesis: An ECB following its estimated pre-crisis rule or a money-growth rule in 2008-2012 would have produced materially smaller output losses.

sources.role: finding: contractionary ECB policy as cause of the euro area Great Recession
method: counterfactual analysis in an estimated New Keynesian model

ideas.test: Estimate a New Keynesian DSGE for the euro area 1999-2013 and simulate counterfactual policy paths with shocks held fixed.
ideas.disconfirming: Counterfactual output paths are close to the actual ones.

ideas.hypothesis: In Indonesia, Islamic bank financing responds less to policy rate changes than conventional lending, so the bank lending channel weakens as Islamic banking grows.

sources.role: setting: Islamic monetary policy transmission in Indonesia
mechanism: transmission effectiveness

ideas.test: Bank-level panel of Indonesian banks 2005-2019; lending growth responses to BI rate changes by Islamic vs conventional status.
ideas.disconfirming: Responses are the same.

ideas.hypothesis: More transparent central banks generate smaller and less variable monetary policy shocks.

sources.role: mechanism: trade-off between room for manoeuvre and predictability
method: identification of monetary policy shocks

ideas.test: Dincer-Eichengreen transparency index for about 20 countries; estimate shocks with high-frequency or VAR methods; panel regression of shock variance on transparency.
ideas.disconfirming: No relation.

ideas.hypothesis: Under real-time adaptive learning, rules with more interest-rate smoothing make convergence to the rational expectations equilibrium faster and more robust.

sources.role: method: real-time learning and convergence to REE under optimal policies
measure: estimated smoothing weights

ideas.test: Simulations of a New Keynesian model with recursive least-squares learning across smoothing values, plus a learning-to-forecast lab experiment; compare convergence speed.
ideas.disconfirming: Smoothing slows or prevents convergence.

ideas.hypothesis: Monetary shocks have long-run non-neutral output effects through TFP, visible as persistent TFP responses 5-10 years out.

sources.role: mechanism: endogenous TFP response to monetary policy

ideas.test: Local projections of utilization-adjusted TFP (Fernald) on narrative monetary shocks over 40 quarters, 1969-2007.
ideas.disconfirming: The TFP response returns to zero.

ideas.hypothesis: Under zero interest rate policy, broad money growth is driven by credit demand rather than base money expansion.

sources.role: mechanism: endogenous money and inefficiency of quantity targets
setting: large excess reserves

ideas.test: Japan and US 2009-2015; Granger causality and VARs among base money, bank loans and M2.
ideas.disconfirming: Base money Granger-causes M2 while loans do not.

ideas.hypothesis: Metros with binding smart-growth constraints have higher shelter inflation and faster pass-through of monetary easing to local CPI.

sources.role: setting: smart growth and new urbanism planning
mechanism: transmission mechanism
mechanism: easing and asset price bubbles

ideas.test: BLS metro CPI 1990-2019 with coded smart-growth policies; local projections of shelter inflation on monetary shocks by policy status.
ideas.disconfirming: No difference.

ideas.hypothesis: Higher fiscal pressure leads the State Bank of Pakistan to set rates below Taylor-rule prescriptions, a sign of fiscal dominance.

sources.role: measure: fiscal pressure
mechanism: monetary-fiscal interaction
method: reaction function estimation

ideas.test: Pakistan monthly 2000-2019; GMM Taylor rule augmented with government borrowing from the central bank.
ideas.disconfirming: Fiscal variables have no effect on the rate.

ideas.hypothesis: High-frequency traffic volumes track output fluctuations, and adding them to real-time reaction-function estimates narrows the gap between real-time and revised output gaps.

sources.role: measure: traffic data in urban research
method: evaluating policy using real-time perceptions
mechanism: output stabilization in policy

ideas.test: FHWA monthly traffic volume trends 1990-2019; nowcast the output gap with and without traffic; compare with final estimates.
ideas.disconfirming: Traffic adds no information.

ideas.hypothesis: During deflation episodes pass-through from currency appreciation to prices is stronger, deepening imported deflation.

sources.role: method: pass-through VAR
setting: deflation and policy efficiency

ideas.test: Panel of about 30 countries; threshold VARs by inflation regime.
ideas.disconfirming: Pass-through is not stronger in deflation.

ideas.hypothesis: Countries with larger foreign exchange reserves experience smaller spillovers from US monetary shocks.

sources.role: setting: reserve accumulation in China
finding: bidirectional China-US spillovers

ideas.test: Emerging-market panel; local projections of domestic rates and output on US shocks interacted with reserves/GDP.
ideas.disconfirming: No attenuation.

ideas.hypothesis: Higher inflation volatility reduces business innovation through uncertainty and relative price distortions.

sources.role: mechanism: monetary conditions and innovation incentives
setting: inflation targeting regime
mechanism: flexible inflation targeting and volatility

ideas.test: Cross-country panel 1980-2015 of patents and inflation volatility, using inflation-targeting adoption as an instrument.
ideas.disconfirming: No relation.

ideas.hypothesis: Tightening during crisis recessions does not raise credibility, measured by anchored expectations, but deepens the recession.

sources.role: setting: IMF tightening prescription
mechanism: credibility

ideas.test: Emerging-market crises 1994-2015; Consensus expectations and policy rate changes; panel.
ideas.disconfirming: Tightening raises anchoring without deeper recessions.

ideas.hypothesis: FOMC decisions deviate more from rule prescriptions when transcripts show more reliance on judgment, and those deviations improve outcomes.

sources.role: mechanism: science and art
method: rule-based evaluation

ideas.test: Text analysis of FOMC transcripts 1976-2013; regress Taylor deviations and later forecast errors on judgment.
ideas.disconfirming: Judgment is unrelated to deviations or worsens outcomes.

ideas.hypothesis: Gains from international monetary coordination are larger when one or both economies are at the zero lower bound.

sources.role: mechanism: need for coordination
setting: ZLB constraints

ideas.test: Two-country New Keynesian calibration plus spillover estimates conditional on ZLB periods.
ideas.disconfirming: Coordination gains are no larger.
